name: Mercedes Benz SSK 1928
description:
The Mercedes-Benz SSK (Super Sport Kurz - 'Super Sport Short') represents the ultimate expression of 1920s high-performance automotive engineering. Built between 1928 and 1932, the SSK was Ferdinand Porsche's masterpiece, designed specifically for racing and wealthy sporting clientele who demanded the absolute pinnacle of performance.

At the heart of the SSK lies a monstrous 7.1-liter (7065cc) supercharged straight-six engine producing 250 horsepower at 3300 RPM and a colossal 562 Nm of torque at just 1900 RPM. The Roots-type supercharger is driver-engaged via a clutch pedal-activated mechanism, providing instant boost when needed. With twin spark plugs per cylinder and a compression ratio of 7:1, the engine was extraordinarily advanced for its era.

The 'Kurz' (short) designation refers to the shortened chassis compared to the earlier S and SS models, measuring just 2950mm. This compact wheelbase, combined with 1700 kg weight, gave the SSK exceptional agility for such a powerful machine. Top speed exceeded 190 km/h - extraordinary for 1928.

The SSK achieved legendary status through its racing successes. Rudolf Caracciola won the 1929 Tourist Trophy and countless hillclimbs, while Manfred von Brauchitsch dominated at circuits across Europe. Only 33 SSKs were ever built, making it one of the rarest and most valuable automobiles in existence.

To drive an SSK is to experience raw, unfiltered power from the golden age of motorsport - a true titan of the pre-war era.
